posts.name: pwatson1974
posts.cooked:
Ok, after squinting, Spite's text is somethinhg like:

Setup: At the start of the game, put Spite's villain character card into play, Agent of Gloom side up.

Remove all 5 drug cards from the villain deck and put them face down in te villain play area. Search the villain deck for the card Safe house and put it into play. shuffel the villain deck.

Game Play: At the start of the villain turn, if there are (H) cards under the Safe House, flip Spite's villain character card. If not, flip a drug card face up.

Whenever a Lab Raid would be played, discard it instead and Spite deals each hero target 3 melee damage.

At the end of the villain turn, Spite deals the hero target with the highest HP (H) infernal damage. If there are more cards under the Safe House than drug cards face up, flip a drug card facwe down.

Advanced: At the end of the villain turn, flip a drug face up.

 

From the looks of it, this Spite flips multiple times as it is otherwise impossible to meet the conditions at the end of the villain turn. At best, the first turn would bring out two victim cards (One from safe house, one from play). However, even if the heroes put both under the safe house, at the end of the second villain turn, when this would be checked, there would still only be two cards under and two drugs in play. At that point, the heroes can't get ahead of the drugs before they flip Spite.

Actually, there is one way. If one of the first two cards is the Good Samaritan, and the top card is a victim and the card played in turn two is also a victim, the players can get ahead of Spite's drugs (presuming there are 5 players, s otherwise, spite would flip). It seems unlikely that this would be common enough to need the end of turn conditions.

Very much looking forward to seeing this for reals.

[EDIT]: Also, my eyes hurt now.

My thinking is that cards that are flipped have no text, and can't be interacted with except through special means.  If they are flipped, they aren't "cards" as such, and therefore are not valid targets of things like Into the stratosphere.
